A: Coronal MRI of the left hand/wrist from a case report of carpal tunnel syndrome showing an anomalous lumbrical muscle occupying the carpal tunnel; the anomalous muscle is the structural cause of median nerve compression but is not in the findings vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. B: Axial MRI at the left hamate hook level demonstrating a bifid median nerve with a persistent median artery and an anomalous lumbrical muscle in a patient with carpal tunnel syndrome; both named findings map to CTS vocabulary entries. C: Coronal MRI of the right hand/wrist showing an anomalous lumbrical muscle in the carpal tunnel in a case of carpal tunnel syndrome; the muscle is the compressive cause and is recorded as a proposed finding. D: Axial MRI at the right hamate hook level showing a compressed (flattened) median nerve with an anomalous lumbrical muscle, the classic site of median nerve compression in carpal tunnel syndrome.
